summary: Unified resource management for prompts, gates, frameworks, and prompt categories. Use resource_type to specify the resource kind, then action for the operation.

toolDescription.description:
🗂️ RESOURCE MANAGER: CRUD for prompts, gates, frameworks, categories.

resource_manager(resource_type, action, id?, name?, description?)

TYPES: prompt | gate | framework | category
ACTIONS: create | validate | preview | update | delete | list | inspect | reload | analyze_type | analyze_gates | guide | switch | history | rollback | compare

PROMPT AUTHORING: validate a complete draft without mutation, then create. Valid prompt content is user_message_template OR chain_steps OR system_message.

PROMPT MAINTENANCE: inspect detail:"full" -> preview preview_action:"update" -> update with expected_version from the receipt -> verify the returned write receipt.

VERSIONING: history (view versions), rollback (restore), compare (diff versions)

CREATION GUIDES:
• >>create_framework - Framework creation with validation
• >>create_gate - Quality gate creation
• >>create_prompt - Prompt/chain creation

parameters.name: resource_type
parameters.description: Type of resource to manage. Routes to appropriate handler. `category` manages a prompt category's `category.yaml` — the directory holding the prompts is NOT the resource, so `delete` removes the declaration and leaves every prompt in place.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Operation to perform. Prompt-only: validate/analyze_type/analyze_gates/guide. validate checks a creation draft without writing. preview renders what update/delete/rollback would do without writing, naming its target in `preview_action`; it is not destructive, so it takes no `confirm`. Framework-only: switch. Versioning: history/rollback/compare.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Resource identifier. Required for create, update, delete, inspect, reload, switch.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Human-friendly name for the resource (create/update).

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Resource description explaining its purpose (create/update).

parameters.name: enabled_only
parameters.description: Filter list to enabled resources only. Default: true.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Required `true` for destructive actions — `delete` and `rollback` both refuse without it. Deletion cannot be undone: rollback cannot restore a deleted prompt.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Audit reason for reload/delete/switch operations.

parameters.name: full_restart
parameters.description: [Prompt] For reload, create, update and delete: restart the server instead of hot-reloading prompts. Default: false.

parameters.name: goal
parameters.description: [Prompt guide] What you are trying to do; the guide ranks its suggested actions against it.

parameters.name: include_legacy
parameters.description: [Prompt guide] Show full details for actions that are not marked working. Default: false.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: [Prompt] Category tag for the prompt.

parameters.name: user_message_template
parameters.description: [Prompt] Prompt body/template with Nunjucks placeholders.

parameters.name: system_message
parameters.description: [Prompt] Optional system message for the prompt.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: [Prompt] Argument definitions for the prompt. `type` is one of string|number|boolean|array|object. `required` and `defaultValue` are persisted to the prompt's YAML; `validation` accepts pattern/minLength/maxLength and is what arms required-argument enforcement at execution.

parameters.name: argument_updates
parameters.description: [Prompt] Update-only: per-field overlay onto EXISTING arguments, addressed by `name`. `name` must match an argument this prompt already declares — no upsert, so adding/removing/renaming an argument still requires the full `arguments` array. Every other field overlays onto the matched entry only when supplied; an omitted field leaves that entry's current value untouched. Mutually exclusive with `arguments` in the same call. Rejected on `create`. Send the same payload as `action:"preview"` with `preview_action:"update"` to see the result first.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: [Prompt] Anchored edits applied server-side on `update`, so one section can be changed without resending the rest. `field` is user_message_template|system_message|description; `old_string` must match the current text EXACTLY (whitespace included) and uniquely, otherwise the update is rejected naming the anchor and its occurrence count; `new_string` may be empty to delete. Operations apply in order. Pass `replace_all: true` to accept a multi-occurrence anchor. Mutually exclusive with `user_message_template`/`system_message` in the same call. Send the same payload as `action:"preview"` with `preview_action:"update"` to confirm an anchor matched before spending a version.

parameters.name: source_workspace
parameters.description: [Versioning] Read version history belonging to a DIFFERENT workspace. `state.db` is one file shared by every project on the machine, isolated by workspace id alone, so another checkout's history is already present and merely filtered out. READ-ONLY and scope-local-on-write: honoured by `history` and `compare`; every other action REJECTS it rather than ignoring it, because a snapshot recorded elsewhere describes files that may not exist here and version numbering is per-workspace. Inspect with it, then apply the change in that workspace.

parameters.name: preview_action
parameters.description: Required with `action:"preview"`, and refused without it — it names WHICH mutation is being previewed. `update` (prompt only): returns the resulting text bodies and the diff, for a full update or a `patch`. `rollback` (prompt|gate|framework): returns the diff between the current state and the version you would restore, and still refuses a version whose snapshot is incomplete. `delete` (prompt|gate|framework): reports what would be removed, including the prompts that reference it. A preview writes nothing, records no version, and needs no `confirm` — it is not a destructive action. `update` is refused for gate and framework, which have no update preview path and would perform the update.

parameters.name: tool_operation
parameters.description: [Prompt] Update-only: how a `tools` change relates to the CURRENT binding. Omit it and a supplied `tools` array REPLACES the binding, so a narrowed array unbinds the dropped ids and leaves their `tools/{id}/` files on disk — the non-destructive default. `add` unions the supplied definitions with what is already bound. `remove` names ids in `tool_ids`, unbinds them AND deletes their directories, and therefore requires `confirm: true`: it is the only `update` that destroys a file the caller sent no replacement for.

parameters.name: tool_ids
parameters.description: [Prompt] Tool ids to unbind and delete. Required by `tool_operation: "remove"` and refused without it, because a parameter that silently does nothing reads as a removal that happened.

parameters.name: unset
parameters.description: [Prompt] Update-only: CLEAR these fields, naming them as the tool parameters you would use to set them. Supplying a value SETS it and omitting it PRESERVES it, so before this there was no way to say REMOVE — `system_message: ""` set an empty body rather than dropping the key, and for the fields the writer carries forward off disk (`tools`, `injection`, `register_with_mcp`, `mcp_prompt_mode`, `subagent_model`, `agent_type`, `composer`) omission was already the preserve signal. Unsettable: agent_type, arguments, artifacts, budget, chain_steps, composer, edges, gate_configuration, injection, mcp_prompt_mode, register_with_mcp, subagent_model, system_message, tools. `name`, `category`, `description` and `user_message_template` are refused by name: they stay settable, but a prompt missing one does not load. Unsetting `system_message` also deletes `system-message.md`; unsetting `tools` unbinds without deleting `tools/{id}/`. A field both supplied and unset in one call is refused rather than resolved in an unseen order.

parameters.name: chain_steps
parameters.description: [Prompt] Chain steps definition for multi-step prompts. Each entry: promptId and stepName required; optional id (kebab-case, minted from stepName when omitted), args, inputMapping, outputMapping, visibility, subagentModel, agentType, framework, retries, inlineGateIds, inlineGateCriteria, delegated, await (node|run — run makes the step detached). Extra keys pass through uninterpreted.

parameters.name: chain_step_operation
parameters.description: [Prompt] Update-only: edit ONE step instead of replacing the whole array. Omit it and a supplied `chain_steps` replaces every step. `add` inserts `chain_step_data` at `chain_step_index`; `remove` drops the step at `chain_step_index`; `reorder` applies `chain_step_order`; `update` overlays `chain_step_data` onto the step at `chain_step_index`, the per-step analogue of `argument_updates`.

parameters.name: chain_step_index
parameters.description: [Prompt] Target index for `chain_step_operation` add (insertion point), remove, or update (step to edit). Zero-based, and refused outside the current step range.

parameters.name: chain_step_data
parameters.description: [Prompt] Step definition for `chain_step_operation: "add"` (the whole step) or `"update"` (the fields to overlay). Same shape as one entry of `chain_steps`.

parameters.name: chain_step_order
parameters.description: [Prompt] New index order for `chain_step_operation: "reorder"`. Must be a permutation of [0..n-1] for the current step count; anything else is refused rather than partially applied.

parameters.name: edges
parameters.description: [Prompt] Dependency edges between this chain's steps, each `{from, to}` naming a step id — an explicit step `id`, or the kebab-case slug minted from `stepName`. Ordering constraints, not control flow: the loader linearizes them into `chainSteps` order at load time. An edge naming a step the chain does not declare, or a cycle, is refused and the write is rolled back — so a `chain_steps` rewrite that drops a step an edge still names must send the corrected `edges` in the SAME call, which is validated as one state. Send `unset: ["edges"]` to drop every edge and keep the authored step order.

parameters.name: budget
parameters.description: [Prompt] Run-level budget for a chain, the same shape and the same caps a submitted Workflow IR declares. A declared structural cap may only NARROW the server default, so a value above it is refused here rather than silently clamped, and an unrecognized key is refused rather than dropped. `pauseOnBlocking: true` HOLDS the run on a blocking unknown until a `gate_action` verb clears it. Send `unset: ["budget"]` to drop the declaration and run on the server defaults.

parameters.name: artifacts
parameters.description: [Prompt] What this prompt's run touches, in the fixed artifact-kind vocabulary (source, test, docs, readme, plan, changelog, config, prompt, gate, pr-body). `produces` names kinds it always yields; `fromArgument` names one declared argument whose value carries the paths this run touches, and must match an argument the prompt declares — the two union. This is the only channel a run has for declaring artifacts, and artifact-scoped gates attach from it. Send `unset: ["artifacts"]` to declare nothing.

parameters.name: tools
parameters.description: [Prompt] Script tools to create with the prompt. Each tool creates files in tools/{id}/ subdirectory. Required: id, name, script. Optional: description, runtime (python|node|shell|auto), schema (JSON Schema object), trigger (schema_match|explicit|always|never), confirm, strict, timeout. Element shape is not constrained at this boundary — it is validated against the script tool schema when written.

parameters.name: gate_configuration
parameters.description: [Prompt] Gate configuration: include (array), exclude (array), framework_gates (boolean — whether this prompt runs its framework's gates; unrelated to the top-level framework_gates parameter, which defines them).

parameters.name: composer
parameters.description: [Prompt] Interactive composer metadata. inputArgument must name a declared string argument; clients may map their current draft only when this field is present.

parameters.name: injection
parameters.description: [Prompt] Prompt-level injection control. Keys: system-prompt, gate-guidance, style-guidance; each takes {enabled?: boolean, frequency?: {mode: every|first-only|never, interval?: number}, target?: steps|gates|both}. A prompt's own declaration outranks the chain or category it runs inside. Omit to leave the prompt's existing block untouched.

parameters.name: register_with_mcp
parameters.description: [Prompt | Category] Whether prompts register as native MCP prompts. On resource_type prompt — FREEZE HAZARD: this value is normally resolved prompt -> category -> global -> default true; setting it writes an explicit prompt-level value that overrides all three permanently, so the prompt stops following any later change to its category or global default. Omit unless this prompt must differ from its category. On resource_type category it writes registerWithMcp into category.yaml, which is that middle level — no freeze hazard, since every prompt in the category still inherits it unless it declares its own.

parameters.name: mcp_prompt_mode
parameters.description: [Prompt | Category] Native MCP prompt behaviour: expand (plain template text) or launch (route through prompt_engine). On resource_type prompt — FREEZE HAZARD: normally resolved prompt -> category -> default expand; an explicit value overrides both permanently and the prompt stops following any later change to its category default. Omit unless this prompt must differ from its category. On resource_type category it writes mcpPromptMode into category.yaml, the default every prompt in the category inherits.

parameters.name: subagent_model
parameters.description: [Prompt] Client-agnostic capability hint for this prompt's ==> delegated steps.

parameters.name: agent_type
parameters.description: [Prompt] Default host agent for this prompt's ==> delegated steps. A step's own agentType overrides it; neither present leaves the choice to the client (Claude Code: general-purpose).

parameters.name: execution_hint
parameters.description: [Prompt] Hint for execution type on creation.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: [Prompt] List filter query.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: [Prompt] Detail level for list/inspect. summary=IDs only, full=complete prompt content.

parameters.name: search_query
parameters.description: [Prompt] Search query for filtering (list action).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: [Gate] Gate type: validation (pass/fail) or guidance (advisory). Default: validation. Writes the gate.yaml key 'type'.

parameters.name: gate_type
parameters.description: [Gate] Gate classification. Default: custom. Writes the gate.yaml key 'gate_type'; 'framework' marks a gate that requires an active framework and is filtered out when framework gates are disabled.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: [Gate] Free kebab-case tag naming what this gate reminds about (e.g. 'code-quality'). An installation's `gates.harnessCovers` (config.jsonc, or config.json) suppresses reminder-tier gates whose subject it lists; check-tier gates (shell_verify, script_tool) are never suppressed. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: [Gate] Severity for prioritization. Default: medium. Omitted on update, an existing gate keeps its current value.

parameters.name: enforcement_mode
parameters.description: [Gate] What a FAIL does: blocking holds the chain step, advisory advances and names the failure in the reply, informational advances silently. Absent, the gate holds a chain step. The strictest gate on a step decides.

parameters.name: block_response_on_fail
parameters.description: [Gate] Withhold the step output when this gate is marked FAIL, returning the gate review in its place. Writes the gate.yaml key 'blockResponseOnFail'. Omitted on update, an existing gate keeps its current value; send `false` to clear it.

parameters.name: evaluation
parameters.description: [Gate] Who reviews this gate: `mode: "self"` (the model that wrote the output) or `mode: "judge"` (a context-isolated reviewer that sees only the output and the criteria). `model` is a hint for which model the judge runs on; `strict` asks for failures first, and defaults to true under `judge`. Writes the gate.yaml key 'evaluation' whole, so a supplied block replaces the existing one. Omitted on update, an existing gate keeps its current block; send `{"mode": "self"}` to return the gate to self-review. An unrecognized key inside the block is refused by path.

parameters.name: guidance
parameters.description: [Gate] Gate guidance content - the criteria or instructions.

parameters.name: pass_criteria
parameters.description: [Gate] Structured pass criteria definitions. Each entry is an object, not a bare string: optional type (inline_guidance|framework_compliance|shell_verify|script_tool) plus the fields that type reads — framework compliance's framework/min_compliance_score/severity/quality_indicators, shell verification's shell_command/shell_timeout/shell_working_dir/shell_env/shell_max_attempts/shell_preset/shell_stdin_source/shell_response_env_var, or script tool's script_tool_id/script_tool_input/script_tool_timeout/script_tool_working_dir.

parameters.name: activation
parameters.description: [Gate] Activation rules: prompt_categories, frameworks, explicit_request.

parameters.name: retry_config
parameters.description: [Gate] Retry configuration: max_attempts, improvement_hints.

parameters.name: framework
parameters.description: [Framework] Framework type identifier. Use action:'list' to see registered frameworks.

parameters.name: system_prompt_guidance
parameters.description: [Framework] System prompt guidance injected when active.

parameters.name: phases
parameters.description: [Framework] Phase definitions: id, name, description, prompts. The advanced fields this description used to fold in are declared as their own parameters below. Element shape is not constrained at this boundary; the framework loader rejects a malformed entry when phases.yaml is read back.

parameters.name: gates
parameters.description: [Framework] Gate configuration: include, exclude arrays.

parameters.name: tool_descriptions
parameters.description: [Framework] Tool description overlays when active.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: [Framework] Whether the framework is enabled.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: [Framework] For switch: persist the change to config. Default: false.

parameters.name: framework_gates
parameters.description: [Framework] Quality gates for this framework, written to framework.yaml. REQUIRED to create a framework. Each entry: id and name (both required), description, frameworkArea, priority (critical|high|medium|low), validationCriteria (array<string>), criteria, severity.

parameters.name: template_suggestions
parameters.description: [Framework] Prompt-enhancement suggestions, written to framework.yaml. Each entry: section (system|user) and type (addition|structure|modification) required; description, content, frameworkJustification, impact (high|medium|low).

parameters.name: framework_elements
parameters.description: [Framework] Section structure expected of a prompt, written to framework.yaml as frameworkElements: requiredSections (array<string>), optionalSections, sectionDescriptions (object).

parameters.name: argument_suggestions
parameters.description: [Framework] Arguments this framework suggests a prompt declare, written to framework.yaml as argumentSuggestions. Each entry: name, type (string|array|object|boolean|number), description, frameworkReason, examples.

parameters.name: judge_prompt
parameters.description: [Framework] Judge-prompt body, written to the file judgePromptFile names.

parameters.name: processing_steps
parameters.description: [Framework] Ordered template-processing steps, written to phases.yaml. Each entry: id, name, description, frameworkBasis, order (positive int), required (boolean); optional section_header and guards.

parameters.name: execution_steps
parameters.description: [Framework] Execution steps with dependencies, written to phases.yaml. Each entry: id, name, action, frameworkPhase, expected_output; optional dependencies (array<string>).

parameters.name: execution_type_enhancements
parameters.description: [Framework] Per-execution-type step overlays (chain vs single), written to phases.yaml.

parameters.name: template_enhancements
parameters.description: [Framework] Written to phases.yaml: systemPromptAdditions, userPromptModifications, contextualHints (each array<string>).

parameters.name: execution_flow
parameters.description: [Framework] Hooks around execution, written to phases.yaml: preProcessingSteps, postProcessingSteps, validationSteps (each array<string>).

parameters.name: quality_indicators
parameters.description: [Framework] Per-phase keywords and patterns for compliance scoring, written to phases.yaml.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: [Versioning] Target version number for rollback action.

parameters.name: from_version
parameters.description: [Versioning] Starting version number for compare action.

parameters.name: to_version
parameters.description: [Versioning] Ending version number for compare action.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: [Versioning] Max versions to return in history. Default: 10.

parameters.name: skip_version
parameters.description: [Versioning] Skip auto-versioning on update. Default: false.

parameters.name: expected_version
parameters.description: [Prompt update] Optimistic concurrency token. Refuses the update before any write/version when the current recorded version differs. Read it from inspect/validate/create/update structured receipts. Cannot be combined with skip_version:true and requires versioning enabled.

commands.summary: Validate and normalize a prompt creation draft without writing files or versions.
Create a prompt/chain with metadata and arguments.
Update prompt fields. Only provided fields change; omitted fields are preserved.
List prompts with filters.
Semantic analysis for execution type recommendation.
Gate configuration suggestions for a prompt.
Get action suggestions for prompt management.
Create a new gate with YAML configuration and guidance.
Update existing gate configuration or guidance.
List all registered gates.
Author a prompt category's category.yaml. Succeeds on a directory that already holds prompts — that is the first declaration, not a duplicate.
Update a category's declaration. Only provided fields change; omitted fields are carried forward from the file on disk.
List every category across the bundled, primary and overlay prompt roots, marking which declare a category.yaml and which have their name and description derived from the directory name.
Create a new framework with YAML configuration.
Update existing framework configuration.
List all available frameworks.
Switch the active framework.
Inspect resource details.
Hot-reload a specific resource from disk.
Delete a resource (with confirmation).
View version history for a resource.
Rollback a resource to a previous version.
Compare two versions of a resource.

validate.message: The 'validate' action is only valid for resource_type: 'prompt'

switch.message: The 'switch' action is only valid for resource_type: 'framework'

analyze_type.message: The 'analyze_type' action is only valid for resource_type: 'prompt'

analyze_gates.message: The 'analyze_gates' action is only valid for resource_type: 'prompt'

guide.message: The 'guide' action is only valid for resource_type: 'prompt'
